📄 Pakistani Interior Minister arrives in Tehran to attend funeral of Iran’s martyred Leader

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has arrived in Tehran to attend the funeral ceremony of the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei.

Iran’s Interior Minister, Eskandar Momeni, welcomed Naqvi in Tehran on Friday.
​
Upon his arrival, Naqvi said, “Iran is our second home, and I have come to Tehran to attend the funeral ceremony of the Leader of Iran’s Islamic Revolution”.
​
He added, “Another delegation, including Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir, Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan, will also come to Iran to attend this ceremony.”
​
Iran began the first stage of funeral ceremonies for the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, with foreign dignitaries and religious figures paying their respects at Tehran’s Grand Mosalla on Friday.
​
Ceremonies will continue on Saturday and Sunday with the body lying in state at the Grand Mosalla before a funeral procession through Tehran on Monday. Further rites are scheduled in the holy city of Qom, followed by ceremonies in Baghdad, Karbala, and Najaf in Iraq, before burial in Mashhad on July 9.

📡 Foreign dignitaries pay tribute to martyred Leader in Tehran

📌 Tehran, IRNA – A ceremony for foreign dignitaries to pay their respects to the martyred leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, began hours ago at the Imam Khomeini Mosalla in Tehran.

The ceremony for foreign high-profile officials to pay their respects to the martyred leader was held on Friday at the Imam Khomeini Mosalla in Tehran.
​
During this ceremony, religious leaders from Russia, India, China, Turkiye, Iraq, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Hungary, and Bangladesh, along with a group of Mujahideen from Iraq’s Kata’ib Hezbollah, gathered to honor the martyred commander of the Islamic Ummah.
​
Additionally, scholars and religious intellectuals from Indonesia and Afghanistan were present, including Ahmad Massoud, the son of Ahmad Shah Massoud. A delegation from Lebanon’s Amal Movement and representatives of the Resistance Front from Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, and Morocco also attended to pay tribute to the martyred leader.
​
Cultural activists from Spain, Ecuador, and Bolivia were also in attendance at the Imam Khomeini Mosalla, honoring the memory of the martyred leader.
​
Ceremonies will continue on Saturday and Sunday with the body lying in state at the Grand Mosalla before a funeral procession through Tehran on Monday. Further rites are scheduled in the holy city of Qom, followed by ceremonies in Baghdad, Karbala, and Najaf in Iraq, before burial in Mashhad on July 9.

🔊 True revenge for martyred Iran Leader is ending US, Israeli oppression of Muslims: Speaker Ghalibaf

📌 TEHRAN, IRNA – Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says that the true way to honor and avenge the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, is to work toward liberating Muslims from the oppression of the United States and the Israeli regime.

Ghalibaf made the remarks during a meeting in Tehran with Khalil Hamdan, a senior member of Lebanon’s Amal Movement, who led a delegation representing Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri at a memorial ceremony for the martyred Iranian leader.
​
Ghalibaf thanked Berri for his message of condolence and recalled visiting Beirut twice during the Lebanon war. He said the martyred Lader had consistently emphasized Berri’s influential role among Lebanon’s Shia community and supported decisions reached through consensus and in the interests of the Lebanese people.
​
Describing the Leader’s martyrdom as a great loss for the Islamic world, Ghalibaf said that preserving Muslim unity and confronting foreign oppression represented the most meaningful tribute to his legacy.
​
He also revealed that he had spoken with Berri three times during the recent US-Israeli war against Iran, saying Lebanon had been a key concern during negotiations with the United States.
​
According to Ghalibaf, Iran insisted on including provisions related to Lebanon in a mutual understanding, arguing that implementing those commitments would strengthen the country and help prevent internal instability.
​
Hamdan delivered a written message from Berri, offering condolences to the Iranian people and praising the martyred Leader’s legacy.
​
He also highlighted the historical roots of the Amal Movement, founded in 1974 by Lebanese-Iranian cleric Imam Musa al-Sadr and Iranian politician Mostafa Chamran, noting their contributions to the early development of the Islamic Revolution’s ideas.

🖥 Ghalibaf meets with senior Amal Movement official in Tehran

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf met with a senior member of the Lebanese Amal Movement, Khalil Hamdan, in Tehran on Thursday.

Hamdan, along with a group of members of the country’s parliament, has traveled to Iran to attend the funeral of the martyred Leader, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei.
​
Also, representatives from Islamic centers, civic groups, and antiwar and anti-hegemony movements from several European countries, including Italy, the Netherlands, Britain, Denmark, and Austria, have traveled to Tehran to attend or provide media coverage of the ceremony.
